chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Sa'd al-Ahwas

He said: I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about praying in the skins of predatory animals, so he said: Do not pray in them. He said: And I asked him, Can a man pray in a silk garment? So he said: No.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in the skins of predatory animals and in silk according to Imam Al-Rida?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the disliked status (karāhah) of praying in the skins of predatory animals and silk, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on modesty and distinguishing attire from that of extravagance. The narration highlights the practical application of these rulings by early scholars like Ismail ibn Sa'd, who sought precise guidance on specific materials for ritual purity and decorum.
